texts.value: Part of major adhesin Nap complex of the attachment organelle which mediates attachment to host ciliated epithelium (PubMed:33057023) and plays a major role in gliding motility (PubMed:40153444). This protein and P40/P90 mutually stabilize each other (PubMed:16385047). The 3 adhesin proteins are required for formation of the attachment organelle (By similarity)
Forms a heterodimer with P40/P90 (PubMed:33057023). The Nap adhesion complex consists of 2 P1-P40/P90 heterodimers (By similarity)
Found on the cell surface, mostly in the attachment (tip) organelle (PubMed:20199607, PubMed:21631602, PubMed:40153444)
Part of an operon with nrnA (MPN_140), P1 (MPN_141) and P40/P90 (MPN_142) (PubMed:16385047). Expressed at high levels in all growth phases in vitro (at protein level) (PubMed:20199607)

The extracellular region has 2 domains; the N-terminus (approximately residues 60-1394) is a 7-bladed beta-propeller where the loops between the blades form a crown (that is partially disordered in the X-ray structure) that projects away from the cell surface (PubMed:33057023, PubMed:40153444). The stalk (approximately residues 1395-1521) links the N-terminus to the transmembrane helix (PubMed:33057023, PubMed:40153444). Both domains are quite mobile (PubMed:40153444)
Loss of expression of P1 as well as downstream P40 and P90; due in part to translational coupling of the 2 open reading frames

The protein is immunogenic in host cells (PubMed:2450165, PubMed:33057023). Antibodies that inhibit cytadherence map to domains in the extracellular region of the protein (PubMed:33057023). Monoclonal antibody (mAb) P1/MCA4, raised against cell membrane proximal residues 1160-1518 inhibits adsorption to host red blood cells and gliding motility on sialylated glass slides, from which cells eventually detach (PubMed:40153444). This mAb has the same effect on M.genitalium cells (PubMed:40153444)

8% of the genome of this strain encodes 5 partial copies of the major adhesion complex (RepMP repeats), variable repeated DNA elements which provide a pool of sequence variation for genes encoding the bacterial surface proteins (PubMed:8948633)
Belongs to the adhesin P1 family
